      "observations": [
        "Both owned diff bodies were read. The new SyncCopyStreamN synchronously copies exactly a uint32_t count, reads at most min(remaining, buffer length), rejects a zero-byte read before completion as NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED, and calls SyncWriteAll for each chunk. Zero count skips stream access. Read and write errors return immediately. It does not return a partial byte count or roll back output already written on error.",
        "The header names the exact-count contract and failure on short input. The while loop follows remaining bytes, std::min bounds each read, and the Buffer owns temporary storage. SyncWriteAll handles partial writes by advancing the pointer and remaining count; the selected helper assumes progress from a successful nonzero write and adds no zero-progress guard. No source test or assertion is added. A future focused test could distinguish exact count, early EOF, partial writes and error after some output, but no test was written or run.",
        "At the fixed accepted revision, a bounded symbol search in mailnews/mail/rust finds no SyncCopyStreamN. Current SyncCopyStream copies until EOF and reports actual bytes; the renamed Exchange multi-message callback uses that helper. These later interfaces do not preserve this exact-count API. The original helper-only commit does not implement offline scheduling, prioritization, or account settings.",
        "Current helper comments explain partial writes; the historical EOF comment explains why zero read is an error. Blank lines before the final return and around read/error/write phases would make the loop easier to scan, as a scoped readability suggestion. No global loop or stream rule is inferred from the sample. No stream IO, EWS download, test, build, lint or accessibility execution.",
